n: Sanctions-evasion settlement networks and sanctions-linked stablecoins
ds: Wholesale cross-border settlement networks serving sanctioned states and their proxies use sub-agent shell companies across third countries, mis-invoiced trade, dedicated VPN and email infrastructure, and sanctions-linked stablecoins to move payments for trade, including dual-use and petroleum goods, outside the reach of sanctions.

src.t: FinCEN (US Treasury), FinCEN Alert on the A7 Network (FIN-2026-Alert007) (2026-10-01)

rat: Corporate trade payments, correspondent flows and stablecoin settlement.

ind.n: Exposure to a sanctions-linked settlement stablecoin or its wrapped versions
ind.cx: Direct or indirect exposure to a sanctions-linked settlement stablecoin, including wrapped versions.
ind.fp: Indirect exposure several hops removed through large exchanges, without other indicators.
ind.ds: The customer offers, has traded in, or has direct or indirect exposure to a stablecoin publicly identified by authorities as part of a sanctions-evasion settlement network, including wrapped or derivative versions.

ind.n: Trade customer pays in stablecoins for commodities not usually bought with digital assets
ind.cx: Importers or shippers pay for petroleum, dual-use or military-relevant goods in stablecoins.
ind.fp: Established digital-asset-native merchants trading goods where crypto settlement is common.
ind.ds: An importer, exporter or shipping customer uses stablecoins for large or high-volume purchases, especially of goods such as military, dual-use or petroleum products that are rarely paid for in digital assets.

ind.n: Payments routed through several shell companies in different jurisdictions before reaching the end recipient
ind.cx: Payments hop through shell companies in several third countries before reaching the end beneficiary.
ind.fp: Legitimate group treasury or commissionaire structures with documented intercompany agreements.
ind.ds: Funds pass through a sequence of apparent shell or front companies across multiple countries with no clear economic purpose before arriving at the final beneficiary.

ind.n: Newly formed entity with vague purpose and large flows
ind.cx: A recently formed company suddenly runs high volumes of large one-off transactions without recurring counterparties.
ind.fp: New businesses may legitimately ramp up quickly; test against business plan and sector.
ind.ds: Recently incorporated entity or group of entities with generic business descriptions shows significant turnover or purchases soon after formation.

ind.n: Trade documents show signs of AI generation or tampering
ind.cx: Invoices show AI-generation or tampering artefacts, out-of-place Cyrillic characters, or analog stamps on digital documents.
ind.fp: Poor-quality scans, translation artefacts or legitimate bilingual documents.
ind.ds: Invoices, shipping papers or certificates show malformed letters, garbled wording, distorted seals or logos, out-of-place characters from another script, or a physical stamp on an otherwise digital document.

ind.n: Invoice amount or format differs from prior invoices
ind.cx: Shipping invoices use templates that differ from those previously seen from the same counterparty.
ind.ds: Victim-side: genuine-looking invoice has altered layout, round figures or inconsistent references.

ind.n: Account accessed through VPN, email or web infrastructure publicly tied to a designated network
ind.cx: Account access or registration emails resolve to VPN or mail infrastructure publicly linked to the network.
ind.fp: Shared commercial hosting or VPN exit nodes used by many unrelated users.
ind.ds: Logins, registration emails or the customer's business website resolve to VPN services, mail servers or IP ranges that authorities have publicly linked to a sanctions-evasion network.

ind.n: OTC or block-trading crypto firm with sudden unexplained growth, thin online presence and short history
ind.cx: A stablecoin OTC or block-trading firm grows suddenly in jurisdictions linked to the network with little public footprint.
ind.fp: Genuine start-ups growing after a funding round or new licence, with transparent ownership.
ind.ds: A digital asset firm focused on stablecoin-fiat pairs, or suspected of unregistered money transmission, shows abrupt unexplained growth linked to jurisdictions of concern while having little public footprint or operating history.

ctl.ds: Traces exposure of deposit and withdrawal addresses to illicit clusters and screens wallets with risk-scored alerts. It reveals on-chain exposure.

Screens customers, owners, counterparties, vessels, dealers and addresses against sanctions, enforcement and restricted-party lists at onboarding and ongoing, using fuzzy matching and secondary identifiers. Potential matches are held for adjudication before service or funds are released.

Routes potential sanctions, proscription or restricted-party exposure to a specialist sanctions or legal team for decision before proceeding, and sets conditions for finance and insurance. It ensures complex legal judgements are made by qualified people.
Screens goods descriptions, HS codes and items against export-control, precursor and procurement watch lists, with access to technical review. It catches proliferation-sensitive and restricted goods.

ctl.n: Counterparty capacity and trade profile assessment
ctl.ds: Tests whether a counterparty's size, history, equipment and sector make the traded volume and goods plausible, and models an expected trade profile to alert on deviation. It detects trading that is out of line with the business.

Aggregates holdings of all designated persons, tests who really controls an entity despite formal shareholdings, and reviews recent ownership transfers and threshold proximity. It prevents ownership-based sanctions thresholds being avoided by splitting or nominee transfers.

Identifies the natural persons who ultimately own or control a legal entity or arrangement and verifies them using independent registers and documents, looking through intermediate layers. It is the core defence against anonymity achieved through layered or opaque structures.
Links accounts, devices, addresses, directors and beneficiaries to surface rings, shared attributes and flow structures that single-account views miss. It supports detection of organised networks.

Tests whether an entity has real operations such as premises, staff, stock and contracts through documents, site or virtual visits, open-source footprint and shell-risk indicators. It helps identify shell and front companies with no genuine activity.

ctl.n: Tightened monitoring for new accounts and entities
ctl.ds: Applies lower thresholds and closer review during the first months of an account or entity and alerts on turnover far above onboarding projections. It addresses the elevated risk at the start of a relationship.

Checks identity and supporting documents for tampering, forgery, template reuse and internal inconsistency, and corroborates their data against authoritative or reliable independent sources. It exposes altered or counterfeit credentials that pass a visual check.

ctl.n: Trade document review and consistency checking
ctl.ds: Trained staff and automated checks review goods, parties, routes, descriptions and codes across invoice, bill of lading and payment documents. It exposes mismatches and falsified paper.

Alerts on repeated or late amendments to consignee, destination, price or parties in a trade, and re-runs due diligence on changed parties. It detects manipulation of documents to evade controls after approval.

Detects use of VPN, proxy and anonymising services and compares access geolocation with declared residence and sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions. It reveals concealed location and supports geographic restrictions.

ctl.n: Counterparty VASP and platform due diligence
ctl.ds: Assesses the licensing, AML controls, jurisdiction and reputation of counterparty exchanges, over-the-counter desks and other virtual asset service providers before enabling flows, and reviews them periodically. It limits exposure through weak or complicit counterparties.

Compares actual activity with the customer's declared profile, history and peers and alerts on material or trend-breaking deviation, usually as a contextual signal. It catches change that rules on fixed thresholds miss.
